**0.11.0 is a breaking release.** It counts usage per stream version in replicated state and exports it per stream on the admin listener, the gateway gives a request time for its size, and the SQLite extension works only with a server of its own release line. 0.11 moves the storage and protocol format to format epoch 7. A 0.11 node refuses epoch-6 Raft WAL directories and object-storage prefixes at startup and refuses 0.10 peers, and a 0.10 node refuses 0.11 peers. The backup format stays 5, so `ursulactl restore` of 0.11 restores a 0.10 backup. There is no in-place upgrade, no rolling upgrade and no rollback.

- **If you cannot move your data yet, stay on 0.10.1.**
- **Deploy 0.11 fresh and move your data with a backup.** Install 0.11 on empty PVCs and never-used object-storage prefixes for the cold store and S3 snapshots, with the 0.10 cluster's `server.cluster_id` and `raft.group_count`. Stop client writes and every SQLite session, back up 0.10 with `ursulactl backup-create` and `backup-verify` of 0.10, stop the 0.10 nodes, copy their cold objects into the 0.11 cold root, skipping `URSULA_FORMAT_EPOCH` and `snapshots/`, and run `ursulactl restore` of 0.11, which checks the copy first. Every restored stream answers with a new `Stream-Incarnation`.
- **A restore keeps each bucket's usage and starts per-stream usage at zero.** With writes stopped, each bucket's committed counters in the first 0.11 `/__ursula/usage` report equal the last 0.10 report's. Every restored stream version starts with zero counters, and a metering consumer starts from cursor `start` in every group once `ursulactl restore` has finished.
- **`helm upgrade` from 0.10 stops at the first pod**, which finds the 0.10 data on its volume and exits. Recover with `helm rollback`. Keep the peer lists of 0.10 and 0.11 nodes apart.
- **`raft.deleted_data_max_age` has a higher floor.** It must leave room for a removed stream's end record to leave within it. With the default install timeout of 120 seconds and the default snapshot drive interval, a value set below 980 seconds with an S3 snapshot store, or 964 seconds inline, refuses to start with `DeletedDataMaxAgeTooShort`, where 0.10 accepted 960. The default of one hour is unchanged.
- **Upgrade the SQLite extension with the server, and stop every SQLite session before the move.** `Ursula-Protocol` now carries the server's release line, `11`, where 0.8 to 0.10 sent `2`. The 0.11 extension refuses a server of another line with `protocol_mismatch` at open and at import, and an answer without `Ursula-Protocol` and `Ursula-Cluster-Id` with `no_server_identity`. Both replace `server_too_old`. The 0.8 to 0.10 extensions refuse a 0.11 server at once with `server_too_old`. A running 0.11 session checks the line only at its next `HEAD`, which it sends to confirm an answer such as a `412` or a `404`, and a running 0.10 session checks only the cluster id, so neither notices the move by itself.
- **Usage is counted per stream version.** Each stream version holds its committed counters and applied appends in replicated state, and `/__ursula/usage` derives each bucket's counters from them, with the version 2 shape and values. A deleted, expired or purged stream leaves an end record with its final usage, at most 65,536 per group. Group snapshots carry each stream version's usage and the end records, and an install requires every bucket's counters to equal its retired usage plus its live stream versions plus its end records, so a replica that installs a snapshot keeps them. A restore refuses a backup that holds a stream but no history event, which no release since 0.8 writes. `/__ursula/metrics` gains `usage_end_records_retired` and `usage_end_records_folded_early`, and `group_state_gauges` the end-record gauges.
- **Per-stream usage export.** `POST /__ursula/usage/streams`, served on the admin listener only, lists per Raft group the usage of each stream version that changed after a cursor, with its counters, its gauges while it lives and how it ended, and relists a group with each bucket's retired usage and totals when the cursor needs it. A metering consumer follows the contract in [Per-stream usage](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/operations#per-stream-usage). `history` in the backup import answer is 16 lowercase hex digits, as in the export, where it was a JSON number, and the purge report names in `groups` each group's purge entry and the history it applied in.
- **End records fold in the background sweep.** Each group's leader folds an end record into its bucket's counters half of `raft.deleted_data_max_age` after the removal, by its own monotonic clock, with the `Sweep` Raft entries that replace `ExpireStreams`. The sweep runs every minute, or every sixteenth of the bound if that is shorter. A node that restarts or installs a snapshot dates the end records it holds then by their removal times, so keep the nodes' clocks in sync.
- **The gateway gives a request time for its size** ([#891](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/891)). `ursulagw` waits for a node's answer for `--response-header-timeout` plus the time the node needs to store or copy the request's bytes at 8 MiB per second: its body, or the parts a snapshot commit copies. A large append, create, snapshot or commit no longer gets `504` while the node still works on it. The VFS waits the same allowance beyond its own 15 s, which counts a commit's parts the same way, so it gives up after a gateway whose `--response-header-timeout` is below 15 s, 5 s by default. A commit waits up to the base plus 128 s, longer than the chart's 45 s gateway drain, so a drain can cut its answer, and repeating the commit gets the answer from its key. An object store slower than 8 MiB per second still needs a higher `--response-header-timeout` (`gateway.responseHeaderTimeoutSeconds`).
- **A bucket purge removes its streams in stream-id order**, so every replica of a group numbers the purge's cold-object cleanup entries alike, and cold GC reclaims every purged stream's objects after a leader change. 0.10.1 has the same issue: on 0.10, repeat a purge until it reports `cold_gc_complete=true`.
- **Rust library APIs.** `ursula_runtime::AppendResponse` loses `stream_append_count`, `GroupSnapshot` replaces `stream_append_counts` with `usage`, `GroupEngine::purge_bucket` takes a `PurgeBucketRequest`, and `GroupEngine` gains the required `stream_usage`. `min_deleted_data_max_age` and `effective_deleted_data_max_age` move from `RaftConfig` to `UrsulaConfig`. `ursula_stream::MAX_COLD_SNAPSHOT_BYTES` and its `ursula_runtime` re-export are removed: use `ursula_headers::MAX_SNAPSHOT_BYTES`, the same 1 GiB. `ursula_headers::PROTOCOL_LINE` replaces `PROTOCOL_VERSION`.

Known issues: the known issues of 0.10, [#411](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/411), [#461](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/461), [#465](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/465), [#496](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/496), [#517](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/517), [#518](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/518), [#561](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/561), [#735](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/735), [#753](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/753), [#754](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/754), [#769](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/769) and [#862](https://github.com/tonbo-io/ursula/issues/862), are unchanged. Every change is listed in the [0.11.0 release notes](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/release-notes#0110), and installing 0.11.0 is described in [Upgrading to 0.11](https://ursula.tonbo.io/docs/operations#upgrading-to-011).
